thread:
sam: Heads-up — after flipping the FP8 kernels on the Mistral 7B family in canary, p95 went up for short-chat workloads. Need quick triage.

maya: ugh, saw that in dashboards. overall token throughput looks fine, but latency for 1-4 token responses jumped. do you have traces?

sam: pasted a short trace. p95 1-token response was 12ms -> 21ms after fp8. pipeline shows extra memcpy + reorder step during KV write.

jordan: likely kv-copy format conversion. fp8 kernels we integrated expect packed layout; runtime inserts a packing pass. that packing is O(N) per token and isn't batched across requests.

tess: confirmed with perf tool: repro command: `./bin/profile --model mistral-7b --quant fp8 --batch 1 --seq 8 --iters 300`. output snip: 
```
mean_lat_ms: 18.3
p95_lat_ms: 21.7
kv_copy_ms_per_token: 2.9
pack_kernel_ms: 3.2
```

maya: interesting — for batch=8 throughput improved but tail stayed high for low-batch. suggests packing cost isn't amortized.

sam: can we change kernel selection to prefer fp16 kv-cache for small batch/short seq and fp8 for long seq/batched? dynamic routing by request shape.

jordan: yes we have a policy layer but no shape-based rule for KV format. we can add a rule: if batch_size * seq_len < 32, prefer kv-fp16 route. will add a perf flag to test.

tess: also worth trying mixed precision where weights are int8/4-bit but activations and kv stay fp16. calibration effect: when we calibrate per-layer scales for fp8 we sometimes add quant noise that causes extra ops for range correction. that can induce reorders.

maya: data point: ran calibration sweep for qwen-7b and saw negligible packing cost because kernel expects interleaved layout so runtime avoided memcpy. model-specific kernel expectations matter a lot.

sam: thumbs up. we should capture these differences in shared model profiles so serving runtime picks config without guesswork. propose a small repo of JSON profiles with keys: preferred_kv_format, kernel_family, batch_thresholds, calibration-mode.

jordan: sketch of profile snippet: 
```
{
  "model": "mistral-7b",
  "quant": "fp8",
  "preferred_kv_format": "fp16_small_batch",
  "kernel_family": "packed-v3",
  "batch_thresholds": {
    "prefer_fp8": 32
  },
  "calibration": "per_layer_histogram"
}
```

maya: make sure profiles include 'packing_cost_est' (ms per token) and 'fallback_kernels' list so optimizer can cost out routing.

tess: +1. also add a flag `force_kv_passthrough` for experiments where we want to retain original layout and have kernel implement in-place quant. helps avoid memcpy for small responses.

sam: CI note — run perf job names: `perf/mistral/fp8/kernelflip-176950`. ci-bot: can you kick a micro-benchmark matrix with combinations: {fp8,int8,4bit} x {kv_fp16,kv_fp8} x batches [1,4,8,16]?

ci-bot: started perf matrix job perf/mistral/fp8/kernelflip-176950 — links: https://ci.internal/redwood/perf/176950 (will post results).

jordan: action items: 1) i'll add shape-based kernel routing rule and profile metric writeouts 2) tess will add packing_cost_est to model profiles 3) maya will run the CI matrix and attach CSV 4) sam will draft a short runbook for canary rollback.

sam: thanks. if CI shows int8 or 4-bit doesn't have the packing penalty, we can temporarily prefer those for short-chat until fp8 kernels get an in-place path.

maya: quick note — calibration affects speed too not just accuracy. per-layer hist bins reduce dynamic range surprises but introduce extra post-scale ops; log those in the CSV.

jordan: ok will instrument runtime to emit `packing_ms`, `calib_postscale_ms`, `kv_write_ms` per request.

tess: once we have CSV, I'll create `sources/configs/quant_profiles/mistral-7b/fp8-profile.json` (draft) and share in #eng-ml.

sam: perfect. ping me when CSV and profile draft are up and I'll roll the canary flag back if needed. :thumbsup:
